body:
The Architecture tab shows a design as a diagram of how the software is structured. A human can read it there and an agent can read it while working. Depends on feature:9d778f6e03dea799 for the page and records, and is built after the UI/UX tab and the design agent.

## Asked for

- Architecture is one of the Design page's two tabs.
- Be flexible: Solace will support many types of diagrams. A flow diagram is a basic form, and sequence diagrams and others will come too.
- Eventually it supports drag and drop and WYSIWYG editing (feature: direct editing).
- The human would consider the same Elmish, Lustre approach for architecture diagrams as for UI/UX.

## From the other agent's plan (direction, not gospel)

- Nodes and edges, each with a stable ID.
- Drawn with the contract view's graph layout.

## Decided

- Nodes and edges are elements: each has a permanent ID, and an agent can name exactly which one it means.
- A node is not limited to a fixed list of things it can represent.
- A design is data, not code, and is reference material; see the milestone.
- There is no text editor. A diagram is created and changed by the design agent until direct editing exists.

## Suggested (cursory, not prescriptive)

- Each diagram names its type, so a new type can arrive without changing the format.
- Reuse the Contracts page's graph layout rather than adding a second one. It uses dagre, in `solace-cli/contracts/src/layout.mjs`, as FFI to that app (D-85). It suits flow diagrams; a sequence diagram will need its own drawing.

## Open

- Whether the tab shows only agent-drawn designs, or can start from the code Solace already knows. Nothing in the conversation asked for the second, so it is left out unless the human wants it.

## Not in this feature

Flow diagrams come first; sequence diagrams and other types are later tasks. Drag and drop, direct editing and notes are their own features.
title: design: Architecture tab
